_purpose: Validates the 10pp gross margin range guardrail (§5.3). A company with narrow margin range across the window should have cycle_position = unknown, Test 2 base-effect check skipped, and signals classified via Tests 3 and 4 instead. Without the guardrail, this company's slow structural decline could be mislabeled cyclical.

analysis_window._note: Gross margin range = max(28.0) - min(22.5) = 5.5pp. Below 10pp threshold. Guardrail fires.

findings.classification_reason: Guardrail fires (margin range 5.5pp < 10pp). Test 2 skipped. Test 3 (sector-relative): gross margin 22.5% within bounds. Test 4 (persistence): 6 consecutive declining periods exceeds cycle_length_years=3. Classification: structural.
findings.evidence: Gross margin 28% -> 22.5% over 6 years, monotonically declining

_expected_math.guardrail: Gross margin range 5.5pp < 10pp threshold -> cycle_position = unknown, base-effect check disabled
_expected_math.fundamentals: profitability 5 (EBIT 4% in 0-10 band) + cash_gen 0 (FCF positive) + leverage 0 (3x below half of 5x threshold = 2.5x... actually 3x >= 2.5x so = 3) ... recalculating: leverage 3 (3x at/above half-threshold 2.5x) + liquidity 0 (ratio 1.7 > 1.5) = 8
_expected_math.signals: Because guardrail fires, Test 2 cannot label this cyclical. Test 4 fires (6 period decline > cycle_length 3). Classification: structural. Signal score: 1 × 5 × 1.0 = 5
_expected_math.overrides: G01 does not fire; neither O1 nor O2 activate

_critical_assertion: The margin_compression signal MUST be classified as 'structural' in this case. If the implementation skips the guardrail and tries to apply Test 2 (base-effect check), it would find that 2020 had the highest margin and could incorrectly label the 2025 signal 'cyclical' — discounting it to 0.3 × 5 = 1.5. The guardrail prevents that.
